verses.1: Rama killed Maricha, the demon assuming the form of the deer as per his will and swiftly took the return path.
verses.2: While Rama was hasting to see Sita, he heard from behind the ghastly howl of a jackal.
verses.3: Rama knew it was the horrible, horripilating cry of a jackal which made him apprehensive . It made him think.
verses.4: 'The way the jackal is howling appears ominous. May Sita be safe without being eaten up by demons
verses.5: 'If Lakshmana listens to Maricha imitating my voice in the form of a deer, he, sent by Sita will come for me at once, leaving her behind.
verses.6: 'If Lakshmana listens to Maricha imitating my voice in the form of a deer, he, sent by Sita will come for me at once, leaving her behind.
verses.7: 'Hence the murder of Sita must have been jointly planned by the demons. Maricha who had assumed the form of a golden deer, took me away from the hermitage to a faroff place where, killed by my arrows, he turned a demon uttering the words, Alas, Lakshmana, I am killed.
verses.8: 'Hence the murder of Sita must have been jointly planned by the demons. Maricha who had assumed the form of a golden deer, took me away from the hermitage to a faroff place where, killed by my arrows, he turned a demon uttering the words, Alas, Lakshmana, I am killed.
verses.9: 'On account of living in this dense forest in Janasthana I have earned enmity with the demons. Will Lakshmana and Sita be safe without my protection? I see many terrible portents.'
verses.10: On hearing the jackal's howl, Rama began thinking how the demon in the form of a deer drew him away. Thus in the midst of apprehensions he reached Janasthana.
verses.11: On hearing the jackal's howl, Rama began thinking how the demon in the form of a deer drew him away. Thus in the midst of apprehensions he reached Janasthana.
verses.12: Dejected at heart, the birds and animals piteously kept the great soul (Rama) to the left and produced a dreadful cacophony.
verses.13: On seeing such dreadfu omens at that time, Rama hurried back to his hermitage.
verses.14: Rama arrived at Janasthana thinking (of the safety) of charming Sita and mighty Lakshmana.
verses.15: He then saw Lakshmana coming towards him with a cheerless face. When the sad, depressed Lakshmana came near, he saw Rama (equally) despondent and griefstricken.
verses.16: In this situation Rama the elder brother rebuked Lakshmana for having left Sita behind in a desolate forest infested with demons.
verses.17: Rama, the delight of the Raghus, took hold of Lakshmana's left hand, and in sadness said these sweet harsh words :
verses.18: O gentle Lakshmana you are to blame for coming here, leaving Sita behind. Alas will she be safe now?
verses.19: O heroic Lakshmana I see many inauspicious omens. I think Sita might have been lost or eaten away by the demons of the forest. There is no doubt about it.
verses.20: O heroic Lakshmana I see many inauspicious omens. I think Sita might have been lost or eaten away by the demons of the forest. There is no doubt about it.
verses.21: O Lakshmana, a tiger among men, will we be able to see the daughter of Janaka, living in a state of total wellbeing? Will we be able to get her back ?
verses.22: O mighty Lakshmana from the way the beasts, jackals and birds too have turned in the bright direction of the Sun, crying in a frightful manner, can we hope princess Sita is safe ?
verses.23: Appearing in the guise of a deer, this demon allured me to a great distance. With much effort he was somehow killed. but he assumed his demoniac form while dying.
